Safeguards — certificates and files from outside

How a certificate import or renewal can never take the web interface down or leak a secret, and how files arriving from outside are name-validated, checksum-verified and kept in separate failure domains.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
📍 WhereAdmin → Certificates (import, ACME, renewals); firmware repository; backup server downloads; System backup
On this page
  • Certificates
  • Files from outside

Certificates#

A certificate change touches the web server that serves SATOM itself, so a bad certificate is a way to lock yourself out.

Guard What it prevents
An import cannot take the UI down A bad paste breaking the web server. The PEM is parsed, the private key must match the certificate, the web server configuration is tested, and if it is rejected the files are rolled back and the server reloaded.
ACME signing runs in a minimal environment Handing the signer the application's secrets. The application's own environment carries encryption keys and the database connection string; the signer gets a curated passthrough instead of inheriting it. Provider credentials travel as environment variables, never on the command line.
Secrets redacted from the stored log and the command preview Credentials surviving in a log or on screen.
A plain argument vector, never a shell string Command injection through the signing command.
Node-local renewal journal Losing the record of a failed renewal on exactly the node that needs it. The journal is deliberately outside the replicated set, because the node that fails to renew may be the one with a read-only database. Each node publishes its own journal, and the renewals page shows both.
A failed renewal is its own alert Finding out weeks later from an expiry warning. A failed renewal raises its own signal, escalating to critical after three failures in a row.

💡Tip

To import, issue or renew certificates, see Certificates. For the certificates nodes use to talk to each other, see Node TLS.

Files from outside#

Guard What it prevents
Every external listing, preview and download resolves through a name validator Path traversal and forged names. A bad device or file name returns 404, not a file.
Firmware from a backup server is checksum-verified on arrival Installing a corrupted or substituted image.
Backup bundles carry a checksum sidecar Trusting a copy before you can prove it is intact.
Copies spread across distinct failure domains One host loss taking out every copy. Copies live on the node, on the standby, on an external backup server and in your own download.

ℹ️Note — Placement is part of the guard

The external backup server only protects you if it really is a separate failure domain. Keep it off the hosts that run the primary, the standby and the git server. See Backup server and Fresh installs and known limits.
